reading: FDR froze Japanese assets (+ de facto oil embargo) 26 Jul 1941 -- the act of financial warfare historians credit with cornering Japan toward war. The US market did not move: it did not price the consequence of its own government's weapon.

The market drifted down ~10% through autumn 1941 on the European war and deteriorating US-Japan relations -- war risk was already being priced in aggregate, even though the timing/place of the attack was a surprise.

A genuine surprise attack -- no war scare to price in advance. The day-one drop was modest FOR US ENTRY INTO A WORLD WAR, partly because war risk was already in the price and US entry was survivable/collectable (home territory intact, war production ahead).
The market ground lower into spring 1942 -- Bataan, Singapore, U-boats off the coast -- bottoming 28 Apr 1942 at the point of maximum Axis advance, and turning before Midway (Jun 1942).
